window_count_input_group.description: Rate per EA applies to windows counted by size bucket. Engine sums windows from all active size buckets, applies size bucket modifier, and calculates hours. Rates expressed as EA/hr for a MEDIUM double-hung baseline window.

task_production_rates.name: Floor Protection Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Runner-style drop cloths along window perimeter (brush method) or full radial coverage (spray method). ~12 sec per SF. Same rate as trim floor protection. Spray method uses PS_PROTECT_SF.FLOOR_8FT_RADIUS instead.

task_production_rates.name: Glass Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Masking tape + paper/film on glass panes. Rate in SF/hr of glass area. ~1 min per SF. Single large pane is faster per SF (fewer tape edges). Multi-pane TDL windows are much slower per SF due to many small panes with individual taping. Wide rate range reflects pane configuration variance. Per research A-002: single pane ~5 min/EA, multi-pane TDL ~15-25 min/EA.
task_production_rates.notes: MANDATORY — all methods, all tiers. Largest single protection task for window painting.

task_production_rates.name: Hardware Protection (Remove or Mask)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove or tape/bag window hardware (locks, latches, crank operators). ~3 min per hardware group. Removal slightly slower but produces cleaner finish.

task_production_rates.name: Wall Masking Around Window
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tape + paper masking around window perimeter to protect wall. ~24 sec per LF. Spray method always, brush method only when walls SS_PAINTED_*.

task_production_rates.name: Sill/Stool Protection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tape sill/stool edge to protect finished surface. ~18 sec per LF. Simpler than wall masking (tape-only, no paper). Only when stool is SS_PAINTED_* and method is spray.

task_production_rates.name: Sand Bare Wood Windows

QT3.notes: Sand 150 grit to smooth + final 220 on visible surfaces. ~6 min per window.

QT4.notes: Full 150 → 220 grit sequence. Uniform scratch pattern on all surfaces. ~7.5 min.

QT5.notes: Full 150 → 220 grit. Sand with grain, all surfaces including muntin edges. ~10 min.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Sand bare wood window frame, sash, muntins, extension jamb with 150-220 grit sequence. Rate for medium double-hung. Complex 3D assembly (profiles, edges, recesses) is slower than flat linear trim. Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 3.2.

task_production_rates.name: Fill Defects in Bare Wood

QT3.notes: Fill obvious defects — nail holes, deep grain, damage. ~4 min per window.

QT4.notes: Fill all visible defects at 3 feet. ~5 min.

QT5.notes: Fill every defect that could telegraph through finish. ~6 min.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spot fill nail holes, grain defects, damage on bare wood. Walk rate — most windows need limited fill work in NC (new materials). Rate for medium DH.

task_production_rates.name: Scuff Sand Factory Primer
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Light scuff sand factory primer with 220 grit for adhesion. ~5 min per medium window. Not removing material — creating tooth. Same pace at all tiers (adhesion prep is not tiered). Per research EST-007.

task_production_rates.name: Degrease Metal Windows
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Thorough degreasing with alkaline cleaner (BC-7000 or equivalent). ~4 min per medium window. Apply cleaner, scrub, rinse, verify water-break test. Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.1.

task_production_rates.name: Chemical Etch / Abrasion — Aluminum
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Chemical etch or mechanical abrasion of aluminum surfaces. ~6 min per medium window. Scotch-Brite pad for mechanical abrasion, or apply/dwell/rinse for chemical etch. Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.2.

task_production_rates.name: Rust Assessment and Treatment — Steel

QT3.notes: Remove loose rust and scale. Converter on all exposed steel. ~7.5 min.

QT4.notes: Thorough rust removal per SSPC-SP3. Converter with complete coverage. ~10 min.

QT5.notes: SSPC-SP11 power tool to bare metal where needed. Full converter. Pit filling. ~12 min.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Rust assessment per SSPC standards, mechanical/chemical treatment, rust converter application. Rate varies by condition severity (surface vs scale vs pitting) AND quality tier (thoroughness increases). Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.3.

task_production_rates.name: Clean Prep Dust and Debris
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tack cloth wipe all prepped window surfaces. ~2 min per medium window. Quick pass — same pace at all tiers. Complete dust removal is binary.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Primer Coat
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush primer on all window surfaces (frame, sash, muntins, extension jamb) using 1.5" and 2-2.5" angled sash brushes. ~10 min per medium DH. Slower than finish coat due to bare substrate absorption and careful coverage. Per research EST-007 (~0.4-0.6 hrs/EA total primer pathway, ~0.15 hrs application).

task_production_rates.name: Spray Primer Coat
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray primer via airless (310-411 tip). ~4 min per medium window. ~2.5x faster than brush. Requires additional masking already set up in setup module.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Finish Coat 1
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush finish coat 1 on all window surfaces using 1.5" (sash, muntins) and 2-2.5" (frame, jamb) angled sash brushes. ~17 min per medium DH. Slowest task in the spec — precision detail work on 3D assembly. Coat 1 slower than coat 2 (surface absorption, establishing coverage). Derived from Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 8.3 decomposition.

defect_tolerance.all: No drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. Application quality is NOT tiered. Brush marks sanded out between coats with rigid block (FFD 15.3.1).

task_production_rates.name: Spray Finish Coat 1
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray finish coat 1 (310-411 tip). ~7.5 min per medium window. ~2.3x faster than brush. Coat 1 slower than coat 2 (establishing coverage). Consistent distance and speed for uniform mil thickness. 20-40% material waste from overspray.

defect_tolerance.all: No drips, sags, holidays. No orange peel. Uniform mil thickness. Application quality is NOT tiered.

task_production_rates.name: Inspect Coat (Interstage)

QT3.notes: Quick glance at 6 feet — obvious defects only. ~2.4 min per window.

QT4.notes: Systematic scan at 3 feet — mark all visible defects on each surface. ~4 min.

QT5.notes: Lighted critical inspection at arm's length — zero tolerance on all surfaces. ~6 min.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Visual inspection of applied coat on all window surfaces. Slower per EA than trim inspection per LF because window is a complex 3D assembly (frame, sash, muntins, jamb — all surfaces must be checked). Rates derived from trim inspection rates adapted for EA-based window geometry.

task_production_rates.name: Sand Between Coats

QT3.notes: Spot sand only — visible nibs and rough spots. 220 grit. ~4 min per window.

QT4.notes: Light full sand — entire surface including sash profiles. 220 grit. ~6 min.

QT5.notes: Thorough full sand — all surfaces and muntin edges. 220-320 grit. ~10 min.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Between-coat sanding with rigid sanding block (FFD 15.4.1). Window sanding is slower per unit than trim sanding — 3D assembly with profiles, recesses, and muntin edges requires careful technique vs flat linear trim. Research RF-011.

task_production_rates.name: Patch/Repair Defects (Interstage)

QT3.notes: Repair glaring defects only — deep scratches, obvious holes. ~2 min walk rate.

QT4.notes: Repair all marked defects — visible at 3 feet. ~3 min.

QT5.notes: Repair all defects regardless of size. ~4 min.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spot fill/patch defects found during interstage inspection. Walk rate — most windows need minimal patching in NC. Scope increases at higher tiers.

task_production_rates.name: Spot Coat Patched Areas

QT3.notes: Spot coat obvious repairs only. ~1.5 min walk rate.

QT4.notes: Spot coat all patched areas. ~2 min.

QT5.notes: Spot coat all repairs — ensure uniform film build. ~3 min.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply spot coat over patched/repaired areas. Walk rate — scope proportional to patch scope. Most windows need minimal spot coating in NC.

task_production_rates.name: Clean Sanding Dust (Interstage)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tack cloth wipe all sanded window surfaces between coats. ~2 min per medium window. Same pace at all tiers — complete dust removal is binary.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Finish Coat 2
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush finish coat 2. ~15 min per medium DH. Faster than coat 1 — consistent substrate, no absorption. Same application philosophy: apply, tip once, walk away. Also used for coat 3 at QT5 brush/roll. Per research EST-001.

defect_tolerance.all: No drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. Application quality is NOT tiered.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Finish Coat 2
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray finish coat 2. ~6 min per medium window. Faster than coat 1 — consistent substrate.

defect_tolerance.all: No drips, sags, holidays. No orange peel. Application quality is NOT tiered.

task_production_rates.name: Final Window Inspection

QT3.notes: Quick glance at 6 feet — no obvious defects. ~3 min.

QT4.notes: Systematic scan at 3 feet — all surfaces. ~5 min.

QT5.notes: Critical inspection at arm's length under raking light — zero tolerance. ~7.5 min.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Final quality check of all painted window surfaces. Slower than interstage inspect because final inspection is more thorough — verify sheen consistency, coverage uniformity, sash position (ajar), glass edge quality.

task_production_rates.name: Touch-Up Defects (Final)

QT4.notes: Address all visible defects — blend into surrounding finish. ~4 min.

QT5.notes: Address every imperfection — full coat over spot repairs if needed. ~6 min.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Touch-up defects found during final inspection. Walk rate with spot work. QT5 may require full coat over repair areas to equalize sheen.

task_production_rates.name: Glass Scraping / Cleanup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Score paint edge on glass with sharp razor + putty knife guide, scrape excess. ~5 min per medium single-pane window. Multi-pane (TDL) windows are significantly slower (~12-15 min per window). Wide rate range reflects pane count variance. Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 4.1.1 and research A-004.
task_production_rates.notes: Occurs AFTER full cure (3-7 days for enamels). May happen on a different day than other cleanup tasks.

task_production_rates.name: Reinstall Window Hardware
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Reinstall removed hardware (locks, latches, crank operators) or remove masking from in-place hardware. ~3 min per window. Verify operation after reinstall.

task_production_rates.name: Protection Teardown
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove floor drops, wall masking, sill masking. Rate based on floor protection SF as primary zone. Teardown ~1.5x faster than setup — picking up drops is faster than placing them. Wall/sill/hardware masking teardown bundled into rate. Glass masking removed during glass scrape task (not this task).

task_production_rates.name: Clean Tools
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Fixed time: ~30 min per session regardless of window count. Clean brushes, spray equipment (if used). All waterborne products — water cleanup. Proper storage or disposal of consumables.

quality_tier_effects.description: Standard window painting — baseline for all rates
quality_tier_effects.notes: Standard NC production pace. Per Modifier_Registry QT3_STANDARD = 1.00. Application quality is identical at all tiers — QT3 saves time on inspection scrutiny, sanding discipline (spot only), and repair scope (glaring defects only). Coat count: 2 finish coats.

quality_tier_effects.description: Premium window painting — thorough sanding, full inspection
quality_tier_effects.notes: Per Modifier_Registry QT4_PREMIUM = 1.30. Applied to qt_scaled tasks via explicit qt_rates. Sanding: full 220 grit entire surface. Inspection: systematic at 3 feet. Repair: all visible defects. Coat count: 2 finish coats. Semi-gloss minimum sheen.

quality_tier_effects.description: Superior window painting — maximum care, zero tolerance
quality_tier_effects.notes: Per Modifier_Registry QT5_SUPERIOR = 1.50. Applied to qt_scaled tasks via explicit qt_rates. Sanding: thorough 220-320 grit. Inspection: critical at arm's length under raking light. Repair: all defects. Coat count: 2 coats (spray) or 3+ coats (brush/roll per FFD 15.10.3). Gloss sheen allowed.

additional_rounds.description: QT5 brush adds coat 3 + interstage 2. Coat 3 uses TSK_WIN_BRUSH_FINISH_2 rates (consistent substrate). Per FFD 15.10.3.
additional_rounds.notes: Do NOT enforce spray for QT5 gloss — brush is achievable with proper technique and additional coats.

size_bucket_modifiers.description: Small window — proportionally faster per window
size_bucket_modifiers.notes: Research estimate. Smaller surface area → less time per EA. Applied as inverse modifier on time: effective_time = base_time × 0.75.

size_bucket_modifiers.description: Medium window — baseline for all rates
size_bucket_modifiers.notes: All per-EA rates in this file are calibrated to medium windows.

size_bucket_modifiers.description: Large window — proportionally slower per window
size_bucket_modifiers.notes: Research estimate. Larger surface area → more time per EA.

size_bucket_modifiers.description: Oversized window — use measured perimeter for rate calculation
size_bucket_modifiers.notes: Per-window time scales with perimeter. Use Size Bucket Method: Area = P²÷16. Estimate time from equivalent area vs medium window area. Research assumption A-001.

window_type_modifiers.description: Baseline — most common NC residential window
window_type_modifiers.notes: Doctrine rate: 1.10-1.25 hrs/EA medium. Two operable sashes. Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 8.3.

window_type_modifiers.description: Single operable sash — slightly faster than DH
window_type_modifiers.notes: Doctrine rate: 1.10 hrs/EA medium. One operable sash + crank mechanism. Per Section 8.3.

window_type_modifiers.description: Horizontal sliding sash — similar to casement complexity
window_type_modifiers.notes: Doctrine rate: 1.10 hrs/EA medium. One or two sliding sashes. Per Section 8.3.

window_type_modifiers.description: No operable parts — simplest window type
window_type_modifiers.notes: Doctrine rate: 0.90 hrs/EA medium. No sash mechanisms. Frame + glass only. Faster prep and application. Per Section 8.3.

window_type_modifiers.description: Top-hinged operable sash — similar complexity to DH
window_type_modifiers.notes: Doctrine rate: 1.15 hrs/EA medium. One operable sash + mechanism. Per Section 8.3.

muntin_modifier.description: True divided light (TDL) muntins add +20% labor to application and sanding tasks
muntin_modifier.notes: Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 8.3. Simulated divided lights (SDL) with snap-in grilles do NOT trigger this modifier — grilles are removed before painting. Glass masking is separately affected (more panes to mask).

height_access_effects.notes: Floor-level access. Baseline. Per Modifier_Registry H1_STANDARD = 1.00.
Step/extension ladder required. Per Modifier_Registry H2_TALL = 1.30.
Lift equipment required. Per Modifier_Registry H5_LIFT = 2.50.

modifiers.description: Good condition — minimal prep. Default for NC.
Fair condition — moderate prep. Installation or storage damage.
Poor condition — extensive prep. Significant damage.

condition_modifiers.notes: Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 8.5. In NC, condition is typically Good. Fair/Poor would indicate installation damage, shipping damage, or weathering before enclosure. Finish modifiers remain 1.00x regardless of condition.

crew_configurations.name: Single Window Brush Painter
crew_configurations.notes: One skilled painter handles all window surfaces with 1.5" and 2-2.5" angled sash brushes. Works window-by-window systematically. May need helper for protection setup/glass masking.

crew_configurations.name: Single Window Sprayer
crew_configurations.notes: One sprayer handles all windows. Helper recommended for extensive masking setup. Sprayer focuses on application only.

rate_notes.ea_based_production: All per-window rates are expressed as EA/hr for a MEDIUM double-hung baseline window (brush, QT3, H1, no muntins, COND_GOOD). Modifiers adjust from this baseline: size_bucket × window_type × muntin × height × condition (prep only) × QT (for qt_scaled tasks). Modifier application order does not affect result (multiplicative stacking).
rate_notes.modifier_application: Modifiers increase TIME, not rate. effective_time = base_time × modifier_product. For ea_per_hour rates: effective_rate = base_rate / modifier_product. Modifiers stack multiplicatively: total_modifier = size × type × muntin × height × condition. Example: Large DH with TDL at H2 = 1.40 × 1.00 × 1.20 × 1.30 = 2.184x time for application tasks.
rate_notes.coat_1_vs_coat_2: Coat 1 is systematically slower than coat 2. Coat 1: surface absorption, establishing coverage. Coat 2: consistent substrate, faster pace. Separate task IDs enable distinct rates. Coat 3 at QT5 uses coat 2 rates.
rate_notes.protection_vs_window_rates: Protection tasks (floor, wall, sill) use SF/LF-based rates tied to protection zone area. Glass masking and hardware protection are per-EA or per-SF of glass. Per-window application tasks use EA-based rates with modifiers.
rate_notes.height_distribution: Height modifiers apply per-window using PaintScope height distribution (IN_EA_WINDOW_H1 through H5). Weighted average height modifier = sum(H_count × H_modifier) / total_count. Alternatively, engine can apply per-window for exact calculation.
rate_notes.glass_masking_variability: Glass masking rate has the widest range of any task (30-80 SF/hr of glass area). Single large panes are fast. Multi-pane TDL Colonial windows with many small panes are very slow per SF. The SF-based rate naturally handles this — same SF masking rate, but TDL windows have more total glass perimeter to tape.

assumptions.value: S=0.75x, M=1.00x (baseline), L=1.40x, O=per measured perimeter
assumptions.source: Research estimate — no canonical doctrine values for size scaling
assumptions.note: Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 8.3 rates are for medium windows. Size scaling is a research estimate.

assumptions.source: Derived from Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 8.3 total rates, normalized to DH baseline
assumptions.note: Doctrine provides total rates by type. Modifiers derived by normalizing to DH midpoint (1.175 hrs).

assumptions.value: Individual task rates decomposed from doctrine total rates (1.10-1.25 hrs/EA for medium DH)
assumptions.note: Doctrine provides total rates. Decomposition into per-task rates requires assumptions about time allocation across tasks. Total should sum to ~1.10-1.25 hrs for SS_PRIMED_FACTORY medium DH at QT3 brush.

assumptions.value: Coat 3 at QT5 brush uses same rates as coat 2 (TSK_WIN_BRUSH_FINISH_2 at 4 EA/hr)
assumptions.source: Aligned with trim paint spec assumption
assumptions.note: No separate coat 3 rate defined. Coat 2 rates apply — substrate is consistent after first coat.

assumptions.value: 60 SF/hr of glass area (~1 min per SF)
assumptions.note: No doctrine defines glass masking rates. SF-based rate accounts for pane configuration naturally — TDL windows have more perimeter-to-area ratio.

validation_plan.task: Total time per medium DH (SS_PRIMED_FACTORY, brush, QT3)
validation_plan.method: Sum all task times for a standard factory-primed medium DH window
validation_plan.notes: Must align with Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 8.3 total rates. Includes setup, prep, 2 finish coats, interstage, inspect, cleanup.

validation_plan.method: Time painter brushing finish coat on 5 medium DH windows with 1.5" + 2.5" sash brushes
validation_plan.expected_range: Coat 1: 15-20 min per window, Coat 2: 12-17 min
validation_plan.notes: Verify coat 1 vs coat 2 differential. Exclude protection time.

validation_plan.task: Glass masking time by pane configuration
validation_plan.method: Time glass masking on single-pane DH vs 6-lite TDL DH vs 15-lite Colonial
validation_plan.notes: Verify SF-based rate handles pane configuration variance.

validation_plan.method: Compare production times for Small vs Medium vs Large windows (same type)
validation_plan.expected_range: S ~75% of M time, L ~140% of M time

validation_plan.method: Compare total time for bare wood vs factory-primed medium DH
